dish_name: Greek Baked Chicken Thighs with Orzo
instructions: Heat the oven to 350°F (180°C) with a rack in the middle.

Zest the lemon until you have 1 tsp, then cut it in half. Mince 2 of the garlic cloves. In a medium bowl, mix the zest, 1/2 tbsp juice squeezed from one lemon half, the minced garlic, 1 tbsp of the oregano, 1 tbsp of the olive oil, 1/2 tsp of the salt and 1/2 tsp of the pepper.
Pat the chicken thighs dry, add them to the bowl and turn them until they're coated. Leave them for 20 minutes while you chop.
Meanwhile, finely chop the onion. Cut the zucchini and the bell pepper into small cubes, about 1/3 inch. Mince the last 2 garlic cloves.

Heat 1 tbsp of the olive oil in a 12 inch ovenproof skillet over medium high until it shimmers. Lay the thighs in smooth side down and leave them alone for about 4 minutes, until the underside is golden brown and lets go of the pan.
Flip them and cook the other side for 3 minutes. They'll still be pink inside. They finish in the oven. Transfer them to a plate.
Turn the heat to medium and add the last 1 tbsp olive oil and the onion. Cook, stirring, for about 2 minutes, until it softens.
Add the zucchini and bell pepper and cook for about 3 minutes, until they start to soften. Add the garlic and stir for 30 seconds, until you can smell it.
Stir in the 1 tbsp tomato paste and cook for about 1 minute, until it turns a shade darker.

Add the 1 1/2 cups orzo, the 2 1/2 cups broth, the crushed tomatoes, the remaining 1 tbsp oregano, the remaining 1 tsp salt and the remaining 1/2 tsp pepper. Stir and scrape up the browned bits from the bottom of the pan.
Set the thighs on top with any juices from the plate, and scatter the cherry tomatoes around them. Don't stir them in. Let it come up to a gentle simmer.

Transfer the pan to the oven, uncovered, and bake for 18 to 20 minutes, until the orzo is tender with a little bite left and most of the liquid is gone. A little liquid on top is fine. You're cooking the thighs to 175°F in the middle, so if you have a thermometer, check them there. No thermometer? Cut into the thickest one: it's done when the juices run clear and there's no pink left.
Take the pan out with an oven mitt. The handle will be hot. Squeeze the rest of the lemon over the top. That should be about 2 tbsp. Crumble 1/2 cup of the feta over it and let it sit for 5 minutes.
Taste the orzo. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
Serve it straight from the pan.
method_notes: All three versions brown the thighs first and finish them on top of orzo cooked in the same pan with broth, so the orzo takes up the chicken's juices. RecipeTin Eats (the lead) marinates the chicken in lemon, garlic and oregano, builds the orzo with zucchini, bell pepper, crushed tomatoes, tomato paste and broth, bakes it uncovered at 350°F, and finishes with lemon juice and feta; The Grateful Girl Cooks dredges the thighs in flour and cooks the orzo with white wine on the stove, and Eat Right adds a cinnamon stick and bakes it for 30 minutes. The lead cuts the thighs into bite size pieces; this version keeps them whole to match the dish, so they're browned on both sides and baked a few minutes longer, and the tomato paste is fried a minute before the liquid goes in. The Mediterranean Dish's version (4.86 from about 208 ratings per search results) blocked the reader, so it couldn't be counted.
